Hi Ayla / Tomasz —

We need to capture a short, auditable artifact set for the EU -> APAC failover scenario for OmniCloud private deployments. This is for the SOC2 / customer evidence package and for the legal handoff in EMEA. Please see the minimal requested items below and attach the authoritative files where possible:

Essential asks (please attach or point to a signed URL):
- Auth chain diagram showing which keystore/CMK controls KMS access during a regional switchover (including key policy snippet).
- Signed MOA (memorandum of agreement) or statement-of-work clause that allows temporary APAC execution of EU-origin requests during DR.
- Timestamped evidence of last integrated runbook test (logs or S3 bundle) demonstrating the control-plane route change with assertions for tenant scoping.
- Network ACL / BGP session brief that shows which prefixes are blackholed and which are routed to APAC during failover.

Constraints to keep in mind: cross-border custody cannot exceed 72 hours without explicit legal sign-off; any KMS key material must remain under the customer’s CMK in the EU unless a documented and signed exception exists.

Target timeline: we need the artifacts by EOD 2026-04-29 so we can include them in the readiness package for AcmeCorp (they requested proof for their internal auditors).

I’m attaching the current checklist (residency-evidence-manifest-20260428.pdf) for convenience.

Thanks —

Quick technical notes to supplement Ayla's artifacts — copied below so auditors and infra teams have a short, plain-English explanation:

- Routing & failover mechanics: For the private deployment we run an active/standby model. During a failover the control plane performs a planned withdraw of EU-pop prefixes and advertises them from the APAC edge via pre-provisioned BGP sessions. The community tag prevents accidental global propagation.
- Token chain: Short-lived tokens are signed by the EU vault (KMS does not export keys). APAC nodes present the signed token to the local token verifier (verifier public key pinned in the VPC NAT gateway). Verifier checks signature + issuer timestamp <= 60 minutes.
- Tenant scoping: Each tenant's KV cache is namespaced to the EU project ID. When the control plane reroutes, KV cache cold-start policy prevents cross-tenant leakage; keys are zeroed and rehydrated per tenant in APAC nodes scoped to the tenant project. Evidence: see km-region-mapping.csv for project->cmk mapping.
- Acceptance tests: We ran a staged test on 2026-04-20 (logs in the S3 bundle). The test included request-replay, token revocation, and a forced key-policy read to validate policy enforcement.

Action items I will take:
- Export token issuance CSV and upload to the shared drive (by 2026-04-29 12:00 UTC).
- Produce a short paragraph describing the verifier key pinning process (to include in evidence).

If legal needs exact policy strings I can paste them into the checklist, but prefer we sanitize any tenant identifiers first.

- Karthik
